summary: Macro-orchestration of units over the Graph kernel. A Pipeline is a named graph of Units (Python, Source, Dag, nested Pipeline, and sinks) run by Runner in two phases (plan then execute) with identity-based checkpoints (MemoryCheckpoint, FileCheckpoint), resume/force, retry and empty-output policies, and parallel layers. Value, Identity, Coverage and SourceState model what flows between units; sinks write to parquet directories or Ibis tables.
key_classes: Pipeline — named container of units over a Graph; add(unit) validates inputs
Runner — plan()/execute()/run() with checkpoint, retry, workers and nested pipelines
Unit (Protocol) / BaseUnit — inputs(), identity(), reference_exists(), run(upstream, ctx)
DagUnit — runs a RelationDAG as a unit with database-identity-aware identity
SourceUnit/CallableSource — incremental sources with cursor and coverage
SinkUnit — base for sinks with WriteMode; IbisTableSink and ParquetDirectorySink implement write
Checkpoint (Protocol), MemoryCheckpoint, FileCheckpoint — identity-keyed result records, progress and pending attempts
Lifecycle (UnitLifecycle, SourceLifecycle, NestedLifecycle) — identify/decide/execute/commit strategy per unit kind
key_functions: Runner.run(*, params=None, target=None, resume=True, force=False) — plan and execute
Runner.plan(...) — identify units and build Plan with parallel layers
structural_digest — deterministic digest used for identities
extension_points: Subclass BaseUnit or implement the Unit protocol (lifecycle attribute)
Implement Checkpoint protocol for new stores
